title: Why Time-Saving Tools Often Leave You Busier: Jevons Paradox
alt_title_1: The 1865 Steam-Engine Law Explaining AI Burnout
alt_title_2: Jevons Paradox at Work: How to Actually Keep Time Saved by AI
description_hook: In 1865, British economist William Stanley Jevons showed in 'The Coal Question' that more fuel-efficient steam engines increased Britain's total coal use instead of cutting it. Here is how Jevons Paradox turns fast AI tools into heavier workloads unless you cap output.

scenes.headline: Faster Software, Yet Zero Extra Free Time
scenes.stat_label: THE ECONOMIC PARADOX BEHIND MODERN BUSYNESS
bullets: Email replaced letters -> inbox volume exploded 50x
AI drafts in seconds -> calendars still overflow
scenes.narration: Every decade brings faster software and smarter AI tools promised to hand back our afternoons, yet knowledge workers end up busier than ever.
scenes.source: William Stanley Jevons, The Coal Question (1865)

scenes.headline: William Stanley Jevons's 1865 Coal Discovery
scenes.stat_label: HIGHER EFFICIENCY SPARKED MASSIVE NEW DEMAND
bullets: Watt's improved engine burned far less coal per unit of work
Cheaper steam power made factories multiply coal consumption
scenes.narration: In his 1865 book The Coal Question, economist William Stanley Jevons spotted why: when James Watt's efficient steam engine burned less coal per job, Britain's total coal consumption surged instead of falling.
scenes.source: William Stanley Jevons, The Coal Question (1865)

scenes.headline: Cheaper Drafting Multiplies Low-Value Noise
scenes.left_body: AI saves 5 hours -> fills gap with 10x more emails & slides
scenes.right_body: AI saves 5 hours -> walls surplus off for 1 flagship asset
scenes.narration: Making an input cheaper multiplies demand. When email and AI make drafting messages ten times faster, workplaces quietly generate ten times more messages, decks, and meetings.

scenes.headline: Wall Off Reclaimed Hours Immediately
scenes.stat_subtext: Route saved hours into deep craft or recovery, never busywork
scenes.narration: Beat Jevons Paradox by capping output volume: when automation saves you five hours a week, immediately wall those hours off for flagship assets or real rest.

scenes.headline: Bank Saved Hours Before Busywork Steals Them
scenes.stat_label: CLAIM EFFICIENCY DIVIDENDS ON YOUR CALENDAR
bullets: Keep shallow communication quotas strictly capped
Convert AI speed directly into protected margin
scenes.narration: Never let efficiency gains leak back into inbox volume; bank saved hours into calm leverage.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule applying William Stanley Jevons (1865)
